lines.say: 43.1k stars, for a tool that lets your coding agents keep working after you walk away.
It is herdr, and it calls itself the runtime your coding agents live on.
You start it where the work lives, run your agents, and split them into panes.
When you leave, ctrl+b q detaches, and herdr keeps the terminals running.
Your work does not stop just because you stepped away.
The docs cover session state, supported agents, connecting machines, and remote use.
It is written in Rust, 93.8% of the code, and released under the Apache License 2.0.
The repo has 3.4k forks, and the latest release is v0.9.3.
To start, pipe the install script from herdr.dev into your shell, then type herdr.
With Homebrew it is just brew install herdr, and Windows gets its own PowerShell installer.
If you prefer building it yourself, clone the repo and run cargo build with the release flag.
Send this to someone who babysits their coding agents all day.
